solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fish rest on something sharp

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a pike is a long pointed spear or spike
to perch is to rest on a high spot, as a bird does

explanation.surface: Someone told to sit down on a spike: an uncomfortable seat.
explanation.definitionFit: The zander, a predatory freshwater fish of Europe, belongs to this perch family and is also called by this name.

clue.text: Built — that could be erected?

definitions.note: to ... a house is to build it, and the phrase is a palindrome read either way

indicators.note: in a down clue an erected word is read upwards, and these letters read the same bottom to top

parts.note: to ... a house is to build it, and the phrase is a palindrome read either way

explanation.surface: Constructed: something that could be raised up?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erected' seems to repeat 'Built', but it means turned upright, read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up a building or tent is to construct or erect it.

clue.text: Amorous surprise awfully grim, OK as lips finally parting?

indicators.note: the end of lips parts the scrambled letters, going between them
awfully suggests something made a mess of, so these letters are rearranged
finally takes the last letter of lips

explanation.surface: A romantic surprise turned grim when the lips finally parted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' makes KISOGRAM from GRIM and OK AS; 'parting' puts S in.
explanation.definitionFit: A kissogram is a greeting delivered with a kiss, often a romantic or cheeky surprise.

clue.text: Theatre lifted, producing acting

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre
forming is making or producing

explanation.surface: A theatre raised its game, staging a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Performing on stage is acting in a show.

clue.text: Grass inspiring present thought

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the grass takes in the present word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
to put a case is to present it

explanation.surface: Smoking grass gave inspiration for a present idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputed means generally believed or supposed, as in his reputed fortune.

clue.text: Swine painting himself originally, English painter

parts.note: a hog is a pig
painting is a form of art

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of himself

explanation.surface: An English painter of swine who appeared in his own painting.
explanation.definitionFit: William Hogarth was an 18th-century English painter and satirist, known for A Rake's Progress.

clue.text: One may be in the bar, and also on the counter?

definitions.text: One may be in the bar
definitions.note: a half note is a note value that fills part of a bar of music, and its letters read the same both ways

indicators.note: read the other way, as if counter-wise, the letters are unchanged, so the word must read the same in both directions

parts.words: One may be in the bar
parts.note: a half note is a note value that fills part of a bar of music, and its letters read the same both ways

explanation.surface: A drink perhaps found in the pub, and on the bar counter too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The bar' looks like a pub, but it is a bar of music; 'the counter' is not the pub counter but a reading in the counter direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A half note, worth two crotchets, is a note value that sits in a bar of written music.

clue.text: Steamy thing in film, is this?

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Is this the steamy scene in a film?
explanation.definitionFit: Condensed water vapour that steams up a mirror or window is a fine haze.

clue.text: Near outstanding energy in noise from charger?

indicators.note: read as standing outside, the near word stands around the energy letter

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Nearly outstanding energy in the noise from a phone charger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charger' suggests an electrical charger, but it is a warhorse.
explanation.definitionFit: A charger is a cavalry horse, and a horse's call is a whinny.

clue.text: Temporary to forcibly budge?

parts.note: to make someone do something is to force them
to shift is to budge or move

explanation.surface: A short-term fix: forcing something to move?
explanation.definitionFit: A makeshift arrangement is a stopgap serving for now until something better comes.

clue.text: Adjustment in rates, something shocking?

indicators.note: an adjustment in the word rates reorders its letters

explanation.surface: A shift in interest rates is a nasty jolt for borrowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A stun gun delivering an electric jolt is literally a shocking device.

clue.text: So good work reversed by parasite in bouncer

indicators.note: by means set beside, so the parasite follows
the run of so, good and work is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
OP is short for opus, a work
a tick is a blood-sucking parasite

explanation.surface: A doorman's good job undone by some hanger-on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' turns SOGOP into POGOS. 'Bouncer' looks like a nightclub doorman, but it is a toy you jump on.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring-loaded stick ridden by jumping is literally a thing that bounces.

clue.text: High point, around one of seven likely to vote Conservative?

indicators.note: the vote-likely pieces sit around the day of the week

parts.note: pro means in favour of, so likely to vote for
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
Monday, abbreviated MON, is one of the seven days of the week

explanation.surface: A peak in the polls, around one of seven Tory-leaning voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One of seven' hides a day of the week, Monday.
explanation.definitionFit: A headland of high land jutting into the sea is a high point on a coast.

clue.text: So the horses usually slow starters?

indicators.note: the starters are the first letters of the four words before it

explanation.surface: So the racehorses are usually slow to leave the starting gate?
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs meaning in this way or therefore.

clue.text: Cook deals with quail in Mexican dish

indicators.note: to cook the books is to falsify, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chef handling quail for a Mexican recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A folded tortilla filled with cheese and grilled is a classic Mexican food.

clue.text: Solid record recalled, capturing male on piano

indicators.note: here the piano piece leads and the rest follows it

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

indicators.note: the reversed record captures the male letter inside it
recalled reads the record word backwards, as if called back

parts.note: a diary is a daily record

explanation.surface: A record reissued, featuring a man playing piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns DIARY into YRAID, and M goes inside to make YRAMID.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry this is a solid figure with a polygon base and triangular faces meeting at an apex.

clue.text: Ad I love, right cheeky thing?

parts.note: a poster is an advertisement
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: An advert I love: the right cheeky one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheeky' suggests impudence, but it means having cheeks, of the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom, made of two buttocks or cheeks, is the rear end of the body.

clue.text: He struggled to get away from posh duke in house in Italy

indicators.note: in places the posh duke within the house-in-Italy run

parts.note: taken as written
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
U means upper-class, so posh

explanation.surface: A man wrestled free from an upper-class duke in his Italian villa.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a struggling prisoner; it is the escapologist himself.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Hungarian-American escapologist struggled out of chains, straitjackets and tanks.

clue.text: Not even a queen, I suspect, possessing beautiful skin

indicators.note: the scrambled letters possess, holding inside, the skin of beautiful
suspect, as an adjective, means dodgy, so these letters are untrustworthy and rearranged
the skin of a word is its outermost letters

explanation.surface: A queen, not even-tempered, suspected of having beautiful skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges A QUEEN I into INEQUAE, and the BL from 'beautiful skin' goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Inequable means uneven or not uniform, the opposite of equable.

clue.text: Important time to close packages

indicators.note: packages means wraps around, so the close word encloses the time word

parts.note: to seal is to close up
MIN, a minute, is a short time

explanation.surface: It's time to seal up the parcels.
explanation.definitionFit: Seminal work is highly influential and of lasting importance.

clue.text: Top — or end — of flight?

definitions.meaning: the flat area at the top of a flight of stairs
the arrival of an aircraft back on the ground

explanation.surface: The top or the end of a flight?
explanation.definitionFit: Flight has two senses here: a staircase, whose top is a platform, and air travel, ending in a touchdown.

clue.text: Most industrious transport site frantic

parts.note: a bus is public transport

indicators.note: frantic suggests wild disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The busiest bus depot is a frantic place.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of busy: the most hard-working or occupied.

clue.text: Within foundation, charge ticked off

indicators.note: within places the charge inside the foundation

parts.note: a bed is a foundation layer, as of a road
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: Charged within the foundation, someone got told off.
explanation.definitionFit: To be berated is to be scolded angrily, which is being ticked off.

clue.text: Show attractive person cutting fringe

indicators.note: cutting the fringe trims away the outer letters of the attractive word

parts.note: a sexpot is a sexually attractive person

explanation.surface: A glamorous person getting a fringe trimmed for a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting fringe' strips S and T from the edges of SEXPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An expo, short for exposition, is a large public exhibition or trade fair.

clue.text: Shame about hospital appearing terse

indicators.note: about means around, so the shame word goes around the hospital letter

parts.note: what a pity is what a shame
H is the abbreviation for hospital on maps and signs

explanation.surface: A shame the hospital seemed so curt.
explanation.definitionFit: A pithy remark is brief and to the point, concise.

clue.text: Those beaten when Grand National favourite comes in without backing

indicators.note: the famous horse enters the middle of the reversed word
backing means the word for without is read backwards

parts.note: sans is French-derived for without
Red Rum won Britain's Grand National steeplechase three times

explanation.surface: Those beaten in the race when the favourite comes in unbacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns SANS into SNAS; Red Rum, the beloved 1970s racehorse, goes inside. 'Those beaten' suggests losing horses, but these are drums.
explanation.definitionFit: A small drum with rattling wires underneath is something a drummer strikes.

clue.text: Divorce is capital!

definitions.meaning: to separate or break up as a couple
the Croatian city on the Adriatic was once the capital of Dalmatia

explanation.surface: An exclamation that divorce is wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital!' looks like an old-fashioned cheer, splendid; it is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple who break up are said to separate, and the Croatian port city was Dalmatia's chief town.

clue.text: Test held by inquisitor, a laugh

indicators.note: the answer is held within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An exam held by a laughing inquisitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken exam, as in a language viva, is a test conducted by mouth.

clue.text: Forbid redirection of indirect trains, primarily

indicators.note: redirection sends the letters of indirect on a new course
primarily takes the first letter of trains

explanation.surface: Banning the diversion of trains onto indirect routes.
explanation.definitionFit: To interdict is to prohibit by authority, especially in law.

clue.text: Party political conference ends after a setback for brand

parts.note: Lab is short for Labour, the UK political party

indicators.note: the setback turns the two end letters around, and they come after the party
the ends are the last letters of political and conference

explanation.surface: A party's conference ends after a political setback for its brand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' gives L and E; 'after a setback' reverses them to EL.
explanation.definitionFit: A label is a trade name or brand, as in a fashion or record label.

clue.text: Two boys like George and William, perhaps?

parts.note: Roy is one boy's name of the pair
Al, short for Alan or Albert, is the second boy's name

explanation.surface: Two lads named after princes, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince George and Prince William belong to the British monarchy's family, so they are regal.

clue.text: Try democratic process initially with a payment for sponsor

parts.note: to have a go is to try

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of democratic and process

parts.note: rent is a regular payment

explanation.surface: Try a democratic process first, and pay to sponsor it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsor at a baptism is a person who stands for the child, so a godparent.
